signIn.title: Configure your workspace
signIn.lead: This is the admin app. Everyday work stays in {product} at its usual address.

card.signIn: Sign in with an ID card
card.hint: The ID card is read by the card software on this computer, and it will ask for your PIN. The other sign-in opens the provider's own page instead.
card.failed: That did not complete. Check the card is in the reader and try again.

missing.title: The card software is not running
missing.lead: Signing in with a card needs the ID-software and its browser extension on this computer. Install it, then try again — nothing here has to be redone.

loginFailed.cancelled: The sign-in was cancelled. Nothing happened — you can try again.
loginFailed.provider_error: The identity provider could not complete the sign-in. Try again; if it keeps failing, it is on their side rather than yours.
loginFailed.missing_code: The sign-in came back incomplete. Start it again from here.
loginFailed.expired: That sign-in took too long and has expired. Start a fresh one.
loginFailed.bad_state: That sign-in could not be matched to the one that started. Start a fresh one.
loginFailed.login_failed: The sign-in could not be completed. Try again.
loginFailed.unknown: The sign-in did not complete. Try again.

nothing.title: Nothing here for you to configure
nothing.lead: You are signed in, but no part of this workspace's configuration is yours. An administrator can give you access. Your everyday work is in {product}.

down.title: The admin service is not answering
down.lead: Nothing was changed. Try again in a minute. If it keeps happening, tell whoever runs this deployment: its start check may have stopped it, and its log says why.

page.lead: The configuration of this workspace, carried out as one file and back in.

network.title: The admin app is not open from here
network.lead: This address answers only inside the networks your organisation set for it. Your everyday work is in {product} at its usual address.

assurance.title: This sign-in is not strong enough here
assurance.lead: The admin app asks for a stronger sign-in than the one you used. Sign in with an ID card, or with a sign-in your organisation counts as strong.

export.title: Export
export.lead: Your whole configuration as one file — to keep, to hand to another workspace, or to edit and bring back.
export.failed: The configuration could not be downloaded: {reason}

import.title: Import
import.lead: Drop a configuration file. Nothing is written until you have seen exactly what it would do — and then either all of it lands, or none of it.
import.drop: Drop a file here, or click to choose one

rejected.type: That is not a configuration file — choose the .json file an export downloaded.
rejected.count: Drop one file at a time.

badge.lands: clean — lands only with the rest

note.failed: did not answer, so its part of the document could not be judged
note.skipped: No service in this workspace owns this section, so it is not applied here — the rest of the document can be.

stop.refused: {n} item was refused, so this document cannot be applied — none of it. Change it in the file (the reason says what) and drop the file again. | {n} items were refused, so this document cannot be applied — none of it. Change them in the file (each reason says what) and drop the file again.
stop.failed: A service did not answer, so this document could not be judged. Nothing was written. Preview again in a moment.
stop.bad: This file cannot be read as a configuration document. Nothing was written. Drop a file exported from this screen.
stop.other: The document could not be previewed: {reason}

act.downloadNow: Download the configuration as it is now

applied.head: Applied.
applied.rest: The whole document is in force.

moved.head: The configuration changed after your preview.
moved.rest: Nothing was written. Preview again to see what this document would do now — the new preview shows anyone else's change it would overwrite.

refused.head: Refused at Apply.
refused.rest: Something the configuration itself does not cover changed after your preview. Nothing was written — the refused item below says what.

failed.head: Nothing was written.
failed.rest: A service could not write its section, so the rest of the document was withheld.

rolledBack.head: Nothing of this document is in force.
rolledBack.rest: A service could not write its section after another had written its own, so that one was restored to what it held before.

partial.head: Only part of this document is in force.
partial.rest: A service could not write its section, and restoring the section written before it failed too. Preview again: the new preview shows exactly what is still to land, and applying it completes the document.

other.head: The document could not be applied.

line.applied: {n} change landed, recorded in the history under your name | {n} changes landed, recorded in the history under your name
line.appliedNothing: nothing in it changes this section
line.withheld: clean, not applied because another section did not land
line.refused: nothing of this section was written
line.rolledBack: written, then restored to what it held before this import
line.notRestored: holds this document's section — the restore after the failure did not succeed
line.skipped: not applied here — no service in this workspace owns it

people.title: People & access
people.lead: Who is in this workspace, and what each person holds across it.
people.loading: Reading who is in the workspace…
people.failed: The people of this workspace could not be read: {reason}

arrivals.heading: Signed in, given nothing yet ({n})
arrivals.lead: They can sign in and see nothing until you give them a role or a user type that holds something.

users.machines: Services acting in this workspace ({n}): {names}. They act as themselves and are set up by whoever runs the deployment.

panel.gone: Their history stays. Giving access back is a new invitation.
panel.userTypeNote: Every person has one. It holds workspace-wide boxes only.
panel.chartType: Their position in the chart of authority gives «{type}», which is the one in force while they sit there.
panel.rolesNote: A role given here holds across the whole workspace.
panel.administratorNote: Holds every box of everything this workspace has, without a role, and sets up the workspace. Only an administrator makes an administrator.
panel.takeAllLead: {name} can no longer sign in to this workspace, and loses every role here. What they did stays in the history.

roles.name: Role name
roles.shipped: Shipped with every workspace; its ticks can be changed.
roles.administrators: Administrators hold every box, these included, without a role. They are set in People & access › Users.
roles.noSetup: Setting up the workspace is never a role's: it comes only with the Administrator checkbox.
roles.noVocabulary: The boxes the services declare could not be read, so a role's boxes cannot be changed here just now.
roles.fieldsUnread: The restricted fields could not be read: their boxes are not shown, and saving keeps them as they are.

types.lead: The one thing every person holds, named after the job. A user type carries workspace-wide boxes only.

corporate.label: People who arrive through your corporate login get:
corporate.note: Applied once, at their first sign-in. Changing it later changes nobody who is already here.

said.corporateLogin: Saved: people arriving through the corporate login get this from now on.

refused.lastAdministrator: {name} is this workspace's last administrator. Make someone else an administrator first.
refused.notAdministrator: You are no longer an administrator of this workspace, so nothing was changed. Sign in again to see what is yours.
refused.roleHeld: «{role}» is held by {n} person. Take it from them first. | «{role}» is held by {n} people. Take it from them first.
refused.rolePlaced: «{role}» is still placed by a service on things it keeps. Move those places to another role first.
refused.typeHeld: «{type}» is held by {n} person. Give them another user type first. | «{type}» is held by {n} people. Give them another user type first.
refused.typeIsDefault: New people get «{type}». Choose another first.
refused.typeIsCorporate: People arriving through your corporate login get «{type}». Choose another first.
refused.typeInChart: A position in the chart of authority gives «{type}». Change that position first.
refused.typeNameTaken: Another user type is already called «{name}».
refused.setupBox: That box sets up the workspace, and only the Administrator checkbox holds it.
refused.unanswered: The admin service did not answer, so nothing was changed. Try again.

history.title: History
history.lead: Every change a person made to this workspace's setup, whichever way it was made.
history.notAnswering: {service} is not answering, so its changes are missing from this list.
history.unread: {service}'s changes could not be read ({reason}), so they are missing from this list.

lines.imported: imported a configuration file: {changed} changed, {unchanged} unchanged
lines.importedNothing: imported a configuration file: nothing changed
lines.administratorByOperator: was made an administrator by whoever runs the deployment
lines.administratorOffByOperator: stopped being an administrator, by whoever runs the deployment
lines.administratorSeeded: was made the workspace's first administrator
lines.roleSeeded: set up the role «{role}» the workspace starts with
lines.roleDescribed: changed what the role «{role}» is for
lines.roleTicksRemoved: changed the ticks of «{role}»: took away {removed}
lines.roleTicksBoth: changed the ticks of «{role}»: added {added}; took away {removed}
lines.typeByDefault: was given the user type «{type}», as everyone new is
lines.typeByCorporateLogin: was given the user type «{type}» by the corporate login
lines.typeIsDefault: made «{type}» the user type new people get
lines.corporateLoginCleared: made the corporate login give what new people get
lines.positionAdded: added the position «{position}» to the chart
lines.positionRemovedUnnamed: removed a position from the chart
lines.positionGivesType: made the position «{position}» give the user type «{type}»
lines.positionGivesNoType: made the position «{position}» give no user type
